item.text: The worktree is clean. I’m going to focus on core utility/model code rather than broad UI changes, because a narrow refactor there is easier to validate and less likely to create OSGi dependency churn.

I found a small duplication in `ContentUtils`: binary and character stream copying both own the same cancellation/read/write/progress loop, with only the buffer type and write target changing. I’m checking the test harness before editing so the refactor gets a focused regression test instead of just compiling by inspection.

item.text: The useful refactor here is to centralize the stream-copy control flow while preserving the public overloads. I’m going to keep the binary-specific progress subtask formatting intact and add direct tests for binary and character copying.

I’m going to edit one production file and add one test file under the existing platform test bundle. The refactor will use a tiny private functional interface so the byte and char overloads share the same cancellation/progress lifecycle without changing their public signatures.
I’m about to patch `ContentUtils` and create `ContentUtilsTest`. The tests will use a local progress monitor instead of `VoidProgressMonitor` so they don’t depend on platform shutdown state.
The production refactor is in place. I’m adding focused tests now: one for binary copy progress, one for character copy, and one cancellation case that exercises the shared loop.
The refactor and tests are written. I’m checking the diff and then I’ll run the narrow Maven build for the affected test bundle if the local Tycho setup can resolve dependencies.
